children: , the enterprise-software and cloud-computing giant, dropped approximately 0.9% to $502.59 Tuesday morning as the 10-year Treasury yield closed in on 4.8%. That matters when one of the world's biggest technology companies is spending at full throttle to win the AI race.

Microsoft deployed $41 billion in capital expenditures during its fiscal fourth quarter, including $5.6 billion through finance leases. Roughly two-thirds funded processors, GPUs and other shorter-lived equipment. Free cash flow came in at $19.6 billion, less than half the quarter's reported capital spending.

The balance sheet is not flashing danger. Microsoft produced $55.4 billion in operating cash flow, while Azure revenue rocketed 43%. The shares also sit 13.48% below their $580.87 GF Value estimate, pointing to potential undervaluation. But with risk-free yields near 4.8%, every new data center must work harderand investors will demand faster proof that today's massive AI spending can deliver tomorrow's profits.

title: Microsoft Stock Drops as $41 Billion Capex Meets 4.8% Yields
